super_dome.why_not_final: Performance evidence conflicts. RENDER measured 53-59 fps at 250 m night and 56.7 fps in the follow view inside the dome. My run on the same build (dome_v3.fhsave, dust storm, speed 1) reported fps 41.0 / 1,153 draws at 250 m night and 33.0 fps / 1,115 draws in the follow view inside the dome, process_ms_avg 32.7-38.5. The V5 section 0 budget is >= 45 fps. If RENDER confirms my numbers on a clean run, the rubric cap applies (consistency 0.60, subject 0.72) and it is a performance fix, not an art fix. My method has known weaknesses (fps read right after a screenshot and a few seconds after camera jumps, in a dust storm); see docs/requests/CRITIC-to-RENDER.md 2026-09-30.
what_works: It reads as a city under glass in game: at 120 m night the ring shows many lit windows in several colours, neon bands and the glass frame catching light; the atrium glows. By day the glass has a sky reflection (round-28 fix 7 landed in game).
Floor cutaway works: L5 / L2 / L1 with the floors above, roof and dome hidden; the atrium pool, fountain, park strip and galleries read from above.
Build stages read in game: foundation with crane, scaffolded levels, dome frame, glass, fit-out.
Venues: the Prism Shift cabinet runs RENDER's attract-loop shader (a neon hexagon tunnel) - the egg reads; the club floor tiles and poles light up; the bar has lit bottles.
Follow view inside the dome: a person by the pool with the RESTAURANT and CREDIT signs, loungers and the escalator behind - the resort mood holds at the follow camera.

fixes.fix: Reconcile performance: run render_perf on dome_v3 and dome_v5 at 250 m night and in the follow view with the weather the saves carry; report fps and frames over 50 ms. Budget >= 45 fps.
POI labels (CAVE, METEORITE FIELD, RICH DEPOSIT) draw through the dome walls into the arcade and club views (known). Hide world labels inside an opened building or behind its walls.
Prism Shift screen: the prism ship is not visible in the tunnel (known). Add the ship sprite so the egg reads as Paul's game.
At 250 m in a dust storm the dome is dim and brown (my night250): the storm grade swallows the lit windows. Exempt emissive windows and neon from the storm fog so the dome still glitters in weather.
Bar close-up: the bottles are five plain coloured cylinders on a box; add a back-bar shelf with 3 rows of bottle shapes and a mirror.
RESTAURANT sign still clipped in the follow view ('RESTAURAN' with the T behind the lift frame): move the plate.
Robot dancers and the club tone check still owed.
